references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 24:46|Matthew 24:46] gives exactly the same beatitude: "Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing so when he comes." Luke 12:43 and Matt 24:46 are part of the same speech about the faithful and wise steward.

In [ref:Luk 12:37|Luke 12:37] Jesus pronounces a similar beatitude over those servants whom the master finds watching when he comes. Both verses speak of the blessing upon servants who are faithful and ready at the Lord's coming.

In [ref:Åp 16:15|Revelation 16:15] Jesus says: "Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps their garments on." A beatitude linked to watchfulness and readiness at the Lord's coming, the same theme as in Luke 12:43.

[ref:Jak 1:12|James 1:12] speaks of the blessing upon the one who endures trials and will receive the crown of life. The theme of faithfulness leading to blessing connects with the faithful servant who is pronounced blessed.

[ref:2 Tim 4:8|2 Timothy 4:8] describes the crown of righteousness waiting for those who have loved His appearing. Paul speaks here of the reward for faithful service, corresponding to the beatitude of the faithful servant in Luke 12:43.

In [ref:1 Pet 5:2-4|1 Peter 5:2-4] elders are urged to shepherd God's flock faithfully, and when the Chief Shepherd appears, they will receive the unfading crown of glory. The picture of faithful service rewarded at the Lord's coming is the same as in Luke 12:43.

[ref:Luk 12:42|Luke 12:42] gives the immediate context for the beatitude: it is the faithful and wise steward who provides food to the servants at the proper time. Verse 43 pronounces the blessing upon exactly this steward.

In [ref:Luk 19:17|Luke 19:17] the master says to the faithful servant: "Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities." Here too, faithful service is rewarded at the Lord's return, just as the faithful servant is pronounced blessed in Luke 12:43.

In [ref:Matt 25:21|Matthew 25:21] the master says: "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much." The parable of the talents shares the theme of reward for faithful stewardship with Luke 12:43.
